minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 8, 2015

Note: The September 8, 2015, meeting was not called to order at 5:00 p.m. due to lack of a quorum.
The City Clerk thereupon declared the meeting adjourned due to lack of quorum to September 8,
2015, at 6:00 p.m.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 6:01 p.m., on September 8, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 3, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Schlicht

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Library Card Sign-Up Month

City Council Minutes  1  September 8, 2015
   The City Council received the presentation from Genesis Hansen, Director of Library and
  Cultural Services.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: referring to comments made by the Mayor Pro Tem at the last Council
Meeting, he stated that there was no nasty behavior from Mr. Raths' supporters. Mr. Gilbert also
presented a copy of a July 6, 2015, draft City Council Meeting agenda which contained an item
under Mayor Pro Tem Raths’ name to reconsider the Mayoral position.

Sharon Genton, M.V.: announced that every Wednesday morning from 6:30 to 7:00 a.m., members
of Rock Harbor Church pray, in front of the library, for city officials, law enforcement and
firefighters. She also announced that the congregation desires to become more available within
the community serving at events such as the Walk Against Drugs.

Rudy Padrol and Necole Abboud, M.V.: announced that Rudy's Christmas Tree Lot is seeking the
City's support as their business is a vehicle for fundraising for local schools and non-profit
organizations. This year they are launching a program called Rudy's Christmas Trees for Troops
to support the military.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the Consent
Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 25, 2015, as
  presented.

City Council Minutes  2  September 8, 2015
 6.  Annual Graffiti Removal, Steam Cleaning, Painting, and Sealing Services

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to Bonanza Steam Cleaning, Inc. for the
  period of September 1, 2015, through June 30, 2017, in an amount not to exceed
  $125,000.00; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Bonanza Steam Cleaning,
  Inc. for the period of September 9, 2015, through June 30, 2016, in an amount not to exceed
  $60,000.00.

7.  Records Retention Schedule

  Adopted Resolution 15-41 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Records Retention
  Schedule

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated August 14, 2015 in the Amount of $1,206,051.30

  Mayor Schlicht inquired about payments made to The Bee Man and whether or not bee
  hives are destroyed when removed. She also asked about the City's natural gas vehicles
  and if it would be more cost-effective to continue using the City's own filling station or the
  new facility in Lake Forest. She expressed concern that the City may be competing with
  private businesses by having its own natural gas filling station.

  Operations Manager Jerry Hill responded that most of the bee hives are destroyed due to
  cross pollination issues.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay noted that both natural
  gas stations were paid for with AQMD monies and staff doesn't feel that the City is
  competing with private business. Mission Viejo's facility is behind gates and staff has
  reached out to other public agencies to offer use of the facility but none have accepted the
  offer.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated August 21, 2015 in the Amount of $804,467.93

  Council Member Sachs thanked staff for using as many local businesses as possible.

City Council Minutes  3  September 8, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Laguna Niguel/Mission Viejo Commuter Rail Station—Amendment No. 2 to
  Cooperative Agreement C-9-9271

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concern that the City is funding another regional facility. She
  asked if there were any studies to show how many Mission Viejo residents benefit from
  the commuter rail station.

  City Manager Wilberg provided some history on the location of the commuter rail station
  and stated that he is not aware of any studies regarding the number of Mission Viejo
  residents that would use the facility.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  Amendment No. 2 to Cooperative Agreement C-9-9271 between the City of Laguna
  Niguel, the City of Mission Viejo and the Orange County Transportation Authority
  updating contact information for the City of Laguna Niguel.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

9.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury announced that due to the holiday, the date of the OCTA Executive
  Committee meeting was changed and he will have a report at the next City Council
  Meeting.

City Council Minutes  4  September 8, 2015
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that there are new classes at the recreation centers and she
encouraged residents to visit the city's website for more information. She also encouraged residents
to use the City's cooling centers at the Library and the Norman P. Murray Community Center
during the hot weather. Referring to current events in the nation targeting first responders, Council
Member Bucknum stated that the community needs to come together and support law enforcement
and firefighters. She asked residents to stop and thank Sheriff's deputies and fire personnel when
they see them. She noted that first responders have families and they are our neighbors. She also
thanked Sheriff's department personnel for the great job they did with the last concert at the lake. It
was very crowded but very orderly, thanks to the deputies who were there keeping everyone safe.
Recounting comments made earlier in the evening, Council Member Bucknum stated that all of
the Council Members have experienced the bullying and threats that come to those who run for
and are elected to political office. She said that it was very disturbing to have it happen to her and
to watch it happening to Mayor Pro Tem Raths. She stated that intimidation is coming only one
way and it's disappointing to see it happen over and over again.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs recommended that Rudy's Christmas Trees add a Hanukkah bush to their
offerings. He announced that Mission Viejo Country Club is hosting its annual Fallen Heroes Golf
Tournament which is a great event and it raises a lot of money for first responders.

Council Member Ury

11.  Consideration of two additional Property Assessed Clear Energy ("PACE")
  financing programs: Figtree and California First

  Council Member Ury presented his report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 15-42 Authorizing the City of Mission Viejo to Join The CaliforniaFIRST
  Program; Authorizing the California Statewide Communities Development Authority to
  Accept Applications From Property Owners, Conduct Contractual Assessment
  Proceedings and Levy Contractual Assessments Within the Incorporated Territory of the
  City; and Authorizing Related Actions.

City Council Minutes  5  September 8, 2015
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  *Note: as of the meeting date, staff had not heard back from Figtree.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked his colleagues for supporting his proposal to give the City's
Commissioners a raise at the last Council Meeting. He noted that he has heard overwhelming
thanks from the Commissioners.

Mayor Schlicht

12.  Monitor implementation of Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE/HERO) type
  energy saving finance programs and to validate the performance of promised
  consumer protections

  Mayor Schlicht presented her report.

  Dennis O'Connor, M.V.: offered his volunteer services if a committee is established to
  develop educational materials for residents.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  establish an informal ad hoc committee which will work with the local real estate
  community for the purpose of developing educational information for residents on the
  PACE programs.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Raths and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Schlicht announced that the Mission Viejo Diablos football team took another win and that
made three in a row. She asked about the billboards on the Kaleidoscope building and what exactly
they are advertising. In honor of 9/11, Mayor Schlicht read a quote from George W. Bush: "Time
is passing. Yet, for the United States of America, there will be no forgetting September the 11th.
We will remember every rescuer who died in honor. We will remember every family that lives in
grief. We will remember the fire and ash, the last phone calls, the funerals of the children."

City Council Minutes  6  September 8, 2015
  ADJOURNMENT

 At the hour of 7:02 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
 Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 22, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

 ______________________________________________
 Karen Hamman, City Clerk

 Approved at the meeting of September 22, 2015

City Council Minutes  7  September 8, 2015
